title: Why Do Onions Make You Cry? #onion #science
description:
A whole onion doesn't make you cry; a cut one does. Each cell keeps a harmless sulfur compound and an enzyme apart. Your knife mixes them, and a second enzyme turns the result into a stinging gas that reaches the nerves on the surface of your eye. Tears wash it away. Chilling the onion slows the enzymes.

More on your body: Why do your fingers wrinkle in water? https://youtu.be/dTu9m6gXCck

Sources
- Imai et al. (2002), An onion enzyme that makes the eyes water, Nature 419: 685
- Eady et al. (2008), Silencing onion lachrymatory factor synthase causes a significant change in the sulfur secondary metabolite profile, Plant Physiology 147: 2096–2106
- Lancaster & Collin (1981), Presence of alliinase in isolated vacuoles and of alkyl cysteine sulphoxides in the cytoplasm of bulbs of onion, Plant Science Letters 22: 169–176
